title: MCP Servers That Reach the Outside World
description: Ten recent MCP servers that connect agents to data and systems they cannot invent: B2B records, financial metrics, flights, CAD, and keyword volumes.
tldr: The interesting MCP launches are no longer wrappers around local files. Recent ones hand an agent live B2B records, calculated financial metrics, flight checkout, a reverse-engineered CAD API, image layout rendering, keyword volumes in fifty countries, and a way to check documents for text you cannot see.
content:
# MCP Servers That Reach the Outside World

An MCP server that reads your local files is useful. One that reaches a system the model cannot invent is a different thing entirely, because it turns recall into retrieval — or, better, into calculation. These ten launches all connect an agent to something outside itself.

## Live B2B data inside the chat

[[link:/tools/1977|Vibe Prospecting MCP]] powers your chat with live B2B data, so you can build lead lists, research companies, enrich contacts and personalize outreach from inside your assistant. There is nothing to run locally and no API key to manage: you connect over a single URL and sign in through your browser on first use. You can search companies by industry, size, location and tech stack, then export the full dataset to CSV.

## Numbers that are calculated, not recalled

[[link:/tools/2000|Finance Toolkit MCP]] takes financial calculations out of the model's hands. It exposes 500+ metrics in 22 tools plus three for search, and works the numbers out instead of recalling them, so the same number comes back in any model. Ask twice and you get the same answer, which is not true of a model reciting a ratio from memory. It is MIT licensed, hosted for free or run locally, and works with Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Cursor and others.

## Booking a flight in one sentence

[[link:/tools/1999|Bonbook MCP]] lets you book flights by chatting with Claude: paste one address into Claude's custom connector settings, name it, connect, then ask for a flight in a new chat. Your first booking opens a secure checkout page and after that you can just say which option to book. There is no account or password to create, though it does need a paid Claude plan.

## CAD without an API key

[[link:/tools/1969|Onshape Native MCP]] is an MCP server for AI-assisted CAD in Onshape. It exposes Onshape's native editor commands and browser-authenticated REST calls through a local API, using a small extension connected to your signed-in browser, so no Onshape API keys are required. You hand the agent a document URL or ask it to use the current tab, and it works with Codex, [[link:/tools/1487|Claude Code]] or another stdio client.

## Layouts that compile to one URL

[[link:/tools/1985|Imagor MCP]] adds a template layer to imagor, the image processing server. An agent writes a layout — OG cards, product grids, quotes, testimonials — and it compiles to a single imagor URL rendered by the imagor you already run. One URL per image means there is no asset pipeline to maintain and nothing to store twice.

## Keyword volumes in fifty countries

[[link:/tools/2014|Seodata]] gives agents keyword data: search volume, CPC, competition and similar keywords across 50+ countries. A free account gets 50 lookups a day and 500 a month, and with no account you still get 20 anonymous lookups a day; the unlimited plan is $4.99 per month. The same key works on both plans, so only the limits change.

## Every conference, expo and trade show

[[link:/tools/1997|ConferenceFindr]] is a finder for business conferences, expos and trade shows, with an MCP server. You search thousands of upcoming events across dozens of countries by industry, location, date and ticket price, including filters for free events and price ceilings. It is a reminder that most useful MCP servers are simply a good dataset with a query interface attached.

## Search results with their sources

[[link:/tools/1995|DeepSearch]] is an independent web search client for the DeepSeek API. Once you sign in it returns ranked web results with source metadata, and it is not affiliated with DeepSeek. Source metadata is the part that matters: an agent that can cite where a result came from is checkable in a way that a bare answer is not.

## The text your agent reads and you cannot

[[link:/tools/2023|Hidden Content]] looks for hidden text in documents before your agent reads them. You sign up with GitHub and the key starts with 20 free pages, after which pages are billed individually, and the same key works from a browser extension or an API call, so your assistant can check a document first or your own code can. It is the defensive entry in this list, and the one most teams will need eventually.

## Guidelines as a lookup, not a memory

[[link:/tools/1968|Apple Design HIG Skill]] gives deterministic access to Apple's Human Interface Guidelines for coding agents, design system engineers and MCP clients, shipping as an agent skill, a DocC updater CLI and a stdio MCP server covering 172+ HIG topics, with a scheduled workflow keeping references in sync. Deterministic reference access is the pattern worth copying: the model should not be guessing at a spec that exists.

## What separates the good ones

The servers that earn their place return something the model could not produce on its own — a number that was computed, a record that exists, a page that was fetched — and say where it came from. The ones that merely wrap an API you could call yourself tend to be slower than just calling it.
